yardstick: A disclosure counts as prominent when a visitor can reach it within two clicks of the homepage. This is the yardstick the Dutch AFM applied in its 2026 review of crypto-asset service providers.

checks.title: Authorisation statement
checks.what: The homepage says the firm is authorised under MiCA and by which supervisor.

checks.title: Pricing, costs and fees policy
checks.what: The policy on pricing, costs and fees is public and reachable within two clicks of the homepage.

checks.title: Climate and environmental impact
checks.what: Information on the principal adverse environmental and climate-related impacts of each crypto-asset's consensus mechanism is public and reachable within two clicks.

checks.title: Complaints procedure
checks.what: The complaints-handling procedure is published, free of charge, with a template, and reachable within two clicks.

checks.title: Links to white papers
checks.what: Firms that run a trading platform, exchange crypto-assets, give advice or manage portfolios link the white paper of each crypto-asset they serve.

checks.title: Risk warning
checks.what: Clients are warned of the risks of crypto-asset transactions where the offer is made, not only in a footer.

checks.title: Regulated and unregulated services told apart
checks.what: Products outside MiCA (for example some staking, lending, DeFi or NFT offers) are labelled as such and not presented under the MiCA authorisation.

checks.title: Register entry matches the website
checks.what: The website listed for the firm in ESMA's MiCA register opens the firm's own site, and that site names the registered legal entity.
